question: Could you generate a report that shows the number of delivered orders for each month in the years 2016, 2017, and 2018? Each column represents a year, and each row represents a month
sql:
WITH monthly_delivered AS (
  SELECT 
    CAST(EXTRACT(MONTH FROM CAST(order_delivered_customer_date AS TIMESTAMP)) AS INTEGER) AS month_num,
    CAST(EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(order_delivered_customer_date AS TIMESTAMP)) AS INTEGER) AS year_num,
    COUNT(*) AS delivered_count
  FROM olist_orders
  WHERE order_status = 'delivered'
    AND order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
    AND CAST(EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(order_delivered_customer_date AS TIMESTAMP)) AS INTEGER) IN (2016, 2017, 2018)
  GROUP BY month_num, year_num
),
all_months AS (
  SELECT 1 AS month_num UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 
  UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 
  UNION ALL SELECT 9 UNION ALL SELECT 10 UNION ALL SELECT 11 UNION ALL SELECT 12
)
SELECT 
  CASE am.month_num
    WHEN 1 THEN 'January'
    WHEN 2 THEN 'February'
    WHEN 3 THEN 'March'
    WHEN 4 THEN 'April'
    WHEN 5 THEN 'May'
    WHEN 6 THEN 'June'
    WHEN 7 THEN 'July'
    WHEN 8 THEN 'August'
    WHEN 9 THEN 'September'
    WHEN 10 THEN 'October'
    WHEN 11 THEN 'November'
    WHEN 12 THEN 'December'
  END AS month_name,
  CAST(COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN md.year_num = 2016 THEN md.delivered_count ELSE 0 END), 0) AS INTEGER) AS "2016",
  CAST(COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN md.year_num = 2017 THEN md.delivered_count ELSE 0 END), 0) AS INTEGER) AS "2017",
  CAST(COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN md.year_num = 2018 THEN md.delivered_count ELSE 0 END), 0) AS INTEGER) AS "2018"
FROM all_months am
LEFT JOIN monthly_delivered md ON am.month_num = md.month_num
GROUP BY am.month_num, month_name
ORDER BY am.month_num

## Your task

Question: Could you generate a report that shows the number of delivered orders for each month in the years 2016, 2017, and 2018? Each column represents a year, and each row represents a month

Schema overview (columns per table; use describe_table for types/samples):
olist_customers: customer_id, customer_unique_id, customer_zip_code_prefix, customer_city, customer_state
olist_geolocation: geolocation_zip_code_prefix, geolocation_lat, geolocation_lng, geolocation_city, geolocation_state
olist_order_items: order_id, order_item_id, product_id, seller_id, shipping_limit_date, price, freight_value
olist_order_payments: order_id, payment_sequential, payment_type, payment_installments, payment_value
olist_order_reviews: review_id, order_id, review_score, review_comment_title, review_comment_message, review_creation_date, review_answer_timestamp
olist_orders: order_id, customer_id, order_status, order_purchase_timestamp, order_approved_at, order_delivered_carrier_date, order_delivered_customer_date, order_estimated_delivery_date
olist_products: product_id, product_category_name, product_name_lenght, product_description_lenght, product_photos_qty, product_weight_g, product_length_cm, product_height_cm, product_width_cm
olist_products_dataset: index, product_id, product_category_name, product_name_lenght, product_description_lenght, product_photos_qty, product_weight_g, product_length_cm, product_height_cm, product_width_cm
olist_sellers: seller_id, seller_zip_code_prefix, seller_city, seller_state
product_category_name_translation: product_category_name, product_category_name_english

How this database is organised (written by an LLM from the tables' notes and keys):
olist_orders is the central transaction table, linking customers via customer_id and items via order_id. olist_order_items records individual line items, connecting orders to products through product_id and sellers via seller_id. olist_order_payments and olist_order_reviews also join to olist_orders using order_id. olist_customers provides customer details, while olist_sellers holds seller information. olist_products describes items, and product_category_name_translation maps Portuguese category names to English. olist_geolocation offers location data for zip code prefixes. olist_products_dataset is a redundant copy of olist_products.

Rows (confidence: high): One row per calendar month (across the three years 2016, 2017, and 2018) — exactly 12 (one per month for the three years specified)

  1. Month identifier (e.g., month name or number) (text)
  2. Number of delivered orders in 2016 (integer)

  4. Number of delivered orders in 2018 (integer)
